items.title: In the Buddha’s birthplace, a famous nun’s appointment draws fire
items.desc: Protesters want Ani Choying Drolma’s selection as head of Lumbini’s development trust annulled over questions about her money and her citizenship. She says every question has been answered. The record is less certain.

items.title: Four ways US foreign policy could change if Democrats win in November
items.desc: Trump has also ​withheld or cancelled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore ​funding.

items.desc: The boat was carrying 15 passengers and its operator from Bhojpur to Chatara when it crashed in Dhankuta district on Sunday afternoon, reportedly after its brakes failed.

items.desc: Superintendent of Police Dan Bahadur Thapa explains the security plan, the technology behind it and the police’s fight against illegal betting.

items.title: RSP panel to examine audio as Khagendra Sunar denies allegations of violence against woman
items.desc: The lawmaker has alleged a conspiracy against him, prompting the party’s disciplinary committee to seek further evidence and consider technical analysis of the recording attributed to him.

items.desc: The weather system is expected to affect much of Nepal through Saturday, raising concerns for farmers preparing to harvest paddy and trekkers heading to the Himalayas.

items.desc: Diesel prices have hit record highs since the US and Israel launched a ​war against Iran in February, and global energy costs spiked.

items.title: NPL Season 3 winner to receive Rs15 million as prize money rises
items.desc: CAN expects the tournament’s gross revenue to reach Rs1.5 billion, driven by sponsorships, ticket sales and broadcasting.

items.title: Chitwan farmers face a race against rain and wild elephants
items.desc: Rain forecasts are delaying the harvest in Madi, but waiting leaves ripe paddy vulnerable to elephant raids.

items.title: Tourism resumes in Manaslu after Budhi Gandaki floods
items.desc: A total of 116 tourists entered the Manaslu Conservation Area in a week after flood damage disrupted trekking routes, but access to the Tsum Valley remains blocked.

items.title: Who pays for Nepal’s informal workers’ security?
items.desc: Nearly nine in ten Nepali workers are informal, yet the system built to protect them barely reaches them. Registration alone won’t fix that.

items.title: Can police make you unlock your phone?
items.desc: Seizing a device, searching it and demanding its password are three different acts. Nepal’s laws and police procedures should treat them that way.

items.title: Nepal resumes power exports to Bangladesh after flood disruption
items.desc: Nepal has restarted its 40MW electricity supply through India’s transmission network, using Solu Khola and Kabeli B1 to replace the flood-damaged Trishuli and Chilime hydropower plants.

items.title: From induction cookers to bank records, Nepalis find ways to use AI
items.desc: A municipal official uses ChatGPT to handle household and office tasks, a ride-hailing driver creates social media videos, and a bank employee cuts hours off data checks with AI tools.

items.title: Violence flares in Paris after largely peaceful protests across France
items.desc: Despite largely peaceful rallies against rising living costs and inequality, clashes erupted in Paris and other French cities, prompting a massive security deployment.

items.title: Will Nepal’s lights stay on at 7pm in the winter?
items.desc: The Bhotekoshi flood and the Kaligandaki landslides exposed a grid that depends on a few valleys and on river flow. Winter evenings, when demand peaks and India’s imports stop, will show how much of Nepal’s power is dependable.

items.title: Inside the colourful world of Durga Puja
items.desc: Photojournalist Bikas Rauniar captures the elaborate pandals and artistic displays that define the festival in Kolkata and Guwahati.

items.title: Sudurpaschim spends millions to fight child marriage, yet the practice persists
items.desc: The province has spent Rs12.87 million on prevention programmes in five years, but has never assessed their impact.

items.title: PHP2Shell security flaw forces thousands of Nepali websites offline
items.desc: Government portals, Nepal Rastra Bank’s website and some digital services have been suspended as a precaution after two critical vulnerabilities were discovered in PHP.

items.title: NPL returns with bigger ambitions and global recognition
items.desc: The third season begins in Kirtipur on Monday with ICC recognition, DRS technology and greater scope for international players.

items.title: Houthi attacks raise safety fears among Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia
items.desc: Around 400,000 Nepalis work in Saudi Arabia. Recent attacks have raised fresh concerns about their safety as workers call for better protection and emergency arrangements.

items.title: Nepal opens door to private power traders, but legal hurdles remain
items.desc: The energy ministry has initiated the process of amending the Electricity Act, with a bill forwarded to the law ministry.

items.title: PHP Foundation ‘under-funded’ with one full-time staff member, director says
items.desc: Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation.

items.title: Two Japanese climbers found dead on Gangapurna
items.desc: Hidesuke Taneishi, 40, and Tetsu Hashimoto, 25, went missing at around 7,050 metres while climbing the 7,455-metre peak in Manang.

items.title: Nepali Congress falls short of one-third women’s quota in central committee
items.desc: All 69 women elected to the central committee won reserved or inclusion-category seats, leaving party president Gagan Thapa to nominate at least 30 more to meet the requirement.

items.title: Bay of Bengal cyclone could bring rain, snow to Nepal next week
items.desc: The weather system may affect Nepal from October 28 to November 1, prompting warnings for farmers to protect paddy crops and trekkers to exercise caution in the high Himalayas.

items.title: A look at the Prithvi Highway as Dashain draws to a close
items.desc: Vehicles carry people returning to Kathmandu after the Dashain break, while others travel to visit relatives after receiving tika and blessings.

items.title: Bhandari calls for long-term climate support for vulnerable countries
items.desc: Nepal’s former president Bidya Devi Bhandari urges Himalayan nations to cooperate on glacier monitoring and disaster preparedness, while calling for long-term international support for climate-vulnerable countries.

items.title: Rutherford, Hossain join NPL teams ahead of new season
items.desc: West Indies batter Sherfane Rutherford joins Sudurpaschim Royals after scoring 291 runs for Gujarat Titans in the 2025 IPL, while Bangladesh all-rounder Shamim Hossain signs for Lumbini Lions.
